prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Britain is a great nation heading the wrong way under Labour’s wrong values: too much waste, tax and talk; too little cleanliness in hospitals, discipline in schools, safety on our streets and control at our borders. Conservatives will act, not talk—rewarding people who do the right thing, extending choice, devolving power to families and communities, and tilting the system back toward the victim. We will govern for the forgotten majority and for everyone in our country, with clear accountability for delivery.

- Value for money and lower taxes: wage war on waste, saving £12bn by 2007–08; £8bn to cut borrowing, £4bn for immediate tax cuts. Spend at least as much as Labour on the NHS, schools, transport and aid, more on police, defence and pensions; slow overall spending growth to 4% a year. Halve council tax bills for millions of pensioners (up to £500). Restore the earnings link for the Basic State Pension; keep Winter Fuel Payments and free TV licences.

- Savings and enterprise: Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; strengthen company pensions (opt-out default; use unclaimed assets to protect victims of scheme failures). Cut red tape with departmental regulatory budgets and sunset reviews; end EU “gold-plating.” Restore our opt-out from the EU Social Chapter. Keep the Pound; maintain Bank of England independence.

- Families and schools: flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under‑5 via Working Tax Credit for any childcare chosen; support workplace nurseries and after-school clubs. Restore discipline—heads control exclusions and admissions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; slash paperwork. Money follows the pupil; publish marks with grades; allow international qualifications; slim and de‑politicise the National Curriculum. 300,000 vocational grants (£1,000) for 14–16s; two hours after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools. Expand popular schools with 600,000 places; allow free places at independent schools at state cost. Moratorium on closing special schools. Scrap university tuition fees; abolish Labour’s admissions regulator; help build university endowments.

- NHS: increase funding by £34bn in the Parliament; cut bureaucracy (fewer PCTs; abolish SHAs; prune quangos); scrap targets; bring back Matrons; strengthen infection control and single rooms. Funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals. End waiting lists in this Parliament. Reform dentistry access and offer low monthly cover. Health checks for non‑EU migrants; a bold STI public health campaign. Partnership on social care so no one is forced to sell their home; more respite and choices for carers.

- Crime and respect: 5,000 extra police officers each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners for real neighbourhood policing. 20,000 new prison places; honesty in sentencing; expand rehab to 25,000 residential places; reclassify cannabis to Class B. Robust counter‑terror strategy under a Homeland Security Minister.

- Controlled immigration: British Border Control Police; 24‑hour port surveillance; restore embarkation controls. Australian‑style points system for work permits. Annual overall immigration limit, including a fixed refugee quota; process asylum claims outside the UK; take powers back from Brussels and update international rules.

- Accountability and local power: abolish regional assemblies; English votes for English laws; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%. Return regional powers to local councils; tougher action on illegal traveller camps; review the Human Rights Act. Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership. End the war on motorists; modernise roads; review all speed cameras; longer rail franchises.

- Environment and rural life: protect Green Belts; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; cut VED for low‑emission cars; boost efficiency, recycling and diverse renewables to secure supplies. Free vote to overturn the hunting ban. Back farmers with honest labelling, Little Red Tractor in public procurement, and CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: spend £2.7bn more than Labour on the armed forces’ front line by 2007–08; preserve historic regiments and key warships; keep NATO central. Be honest about war aims; stay committed to rebuilding Iraq and to a two‑state Middle East peace. No to the Euro and the EU Constitution (referendum within six months); restore Social Chapter opt‑out; repatriate fisheries; support enlargement including Turkey. Meet 0.7% aid target by 2013 with more British control; champion free trade, property rights and the rule of law.

Day One actions:
- Start recruiting 5,000 extra police officers a year.
- Bring back Matron and start delivering cleaner, infection‑free wards.
- First Budget: cut waste, stop Labour’s tax rises, and lower taxes.
- Give heads the power to expel disruptive pupils.
- Begin 24‑hour surveillance at ports of entry.
- Set the date for an EU Constitution referendum and campaign for “No.”
